cards.text: Friend, we're on the road with Paul and his companions. They set sail from Paphos and land at Perga in Pamphylia. And right there, one of the crew, a man named John, leaves them.

cards.question: John leaves Paul and his companions at Perga. Where does he go?

cards.text: The rest of them travel inland from Perga to Pisidian Antioch, and I get winded walking from my oven to the cookie box. Then the Sabbath comes around.

cards.question: True or false: On the Sabbath in Pisidian Antioch, Paul and his companions go into the synagogue and sit down.

cards.text: So there they sit. First comes the reading from the Law and the Prophets, and then the synagogue leaders send word over to them.

cards.question: The synagogue leaders tell Paul and his companions, “Brothers, if you have a word of ___ for the people, please speak.”

cards.text: Paul stands up, motions with his hand and begins: “Men of Israel and you Gentiles who fear God, listen to me!”
And Paul doesn't open with a joke like I would. He goes WAY back: the God of Israel chose their fathers, made them a great people in Egypt and led them out with an uplifted arm.

cards.question: True or false: In Paul's history of Israel, God endures the people's conduct in the wilderness for about forty years.

cards.text: God vanquishes seven nations in Canaan and gives their land to His people as an inheritance. All that takes about 450 years, and then God gives them judges until the time of Samuel the prophet.

cards.question: After the time of the judges, the people of Israel ask for a ___.

cards.text: God gives them Saul son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin, and Saul rules forty years. Then God removes Saul.

cards.question: Paul says God removed Saul. Who does God raise up as Israel's king after him?

cards.text: From David's descendants, God has brought Israel the Savior Jesus, as He promised. Before Jesus arrived, John preached a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel, and no, not the John who went home.

cards.question: As John is completing his course, he says One is coming after him whose ___ he is not worthy to untie.

cards.text: Then Paul tells his listeners that it is to us this message of salvation has been sent. The people of Jerusalem and their rulers didn't recognize Jesus, yet in condemning Him they fulfilled the words of the prophets read every Sabbath.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the people of Jerusalem and their rulers found solid ground for a death sentence against Jesus.

cards.text: No ground at all, and they still asked Pilate to have Him executed. Once they had carried out all that was written about Him, they took Him down from the tree and laid Him in a tomb.

cards.question: True or false: Paul tells the synagogue that Jesus stayed in that tomb.
Paul says God raised Jesus from the dead, and for many days He was seen. Who saw Him?

answers.text: Those who came with Him from Galilee
The rulers who condemned Him in Jerusalem
The synagogue leaders of Pisidian Antioch

cards.text: That's the good news, Paul says: what God promised their fathers, He has fulfilled for their children by raising up Jesus. Then Paul pulls from the Psalms, including this one: “You will not let Your Holy One see decay.”

cards.question: Paul says David served God's purpose in his generation, fell asleep, was buried and saw decay. So who does Paul say did not see decay?

answers.text: The One God raised from the dead
Saul son of Kish from Benjamin

cards.text: Then Paul brings it home: through Jesus, the forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to them. I've been forgiven for a lot of crooked stamps, friend, but nobody ever PROCLAIMED it.

cards.question: Paul says that through Jesus, everyone who believes is justified from everything they could not be justified from by the law of ___.
Paul ends with a warning from the prophets and tells his listeners to watch out that it doesn't happen to them. Who does the prophets' warning call out?

cards.text: Sermon's over. As Paul and his partner Barnabas are leaving the synagogue, the people stop them.

cards.question: What do the people urge Paul and Barnabas to do as they leave the synagogue?

answers.text: Continue this message on the next Sabbath
Leave the city before the next Sabbath
Write this message down for the leaders

cards.text: After the synagogue is dismissed, many of the Jews and devout converts to Judaism follow Paul and Barnabas. The two of them talk with these followers.

cards.question: Paul and Barnabas urge the Jews and converts who followed them to continue in the ___ of God.

cards.text: The following Sabbath, NEARLY THE WHOLE CITY gathers to hear the word of the Lord. Friend, I can't get three bakers to show up for a taste test.

cards.question: When the Jews see the crowds gathered to hear Paul, they are filled with ___.

cards.text: They blasphemously contradict what Paul is saying. But Paul and Barnabas answer them boldly: it was necessary to speak the word of God to them first.

cards.question: Since those Jews reject the word and don't consider themselves worthy of eternal life, who do Paul and Barnabas say they will turn to now?

cards.text: And they back it up with Scripture: “I have made you a light for the Gentiles, to bring salvation to the ends of the earth.”

cards.question: True or false: Paul and Barnabas say turning to the Gentiles is what the Lord has commanded them.
How do the Gentiles in Pisidian Antioch react when they hear Paul and Barnabas say this?

answers.text: They rejoice and glorify the word of the Lord
They ask for a sign before they will listen
They stay quiet and wait for the leaders

cards.text: And all who were appointed for eternal life believed. Whole new batch of believers, fresh out of the oven.

cards.question: True or false: The word of the Lord stays inside the city of Pisidian Antioch.

cards.text: But the Jews incite the religious women of prominence and the leading men of the city. Uh oh.

cards.question: The leading men and prominent women of the city stir up persecution against Paul and Barnabas. What happens to the two of them?

answers.text: They are driven out of the district
They are locked in the city jail
They are sent back to Jerusalem

cards.text: So Paul and Barnabas shake the dust off their feet in protest against them. Then they hit the road again.

cards.question: With the dust shaken off their feet, Paul and Barnabas go to ___.

cards.text: And the disciples are filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit. Keep your apron on, friend, because this road trip is far from over.
